title: Work ethic: stocking shelves and growing up in the grocery
summary: Everyone worked; he stacked shelves, earned candy by behaving, and was punished for throwing clay.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: No. Didn't take, take on. Uh, when you were young, when you were around the, the, the barroom and the grocery, did, did you, did you work at the grocery as a kid?

Oh, sure. That was another thing my father and mother taught me. Everybody works. So, as a, as a small child, when I came home in the evening from school, as a small child, I stacked soap on the lower shelf because I couldn't reach anything else. Right. I put soup up on the middle shelf and maybe, as I got taller, I put cereal on the top shelf. But everybody worked. Uh-huh. And I was, I was made to understand that, that you worked. Don't, never mind your daddy owns a grocery store. That has nothing to do with your life. Yeah, right. You work. And you understand why people work. So the work ethic. The work ethic was. The work ethic was there. Was there. There was no question about it. And in fact, it's, it was part of my life. Right. I didn't, I wasn't told this is the work ethic. Uh-huh. I lived it. You knew it.
